tweetText: Insilico Medicine is moving its AI-developed drug for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis to Phase III trials. This is a key step in proving AI's potential in drug development and could lead to new treatments for serious lung conditions. via AI News.

L’Oreal is leveraging AI to speed up product development and find new uses for existing ingredients. This innovation could lead to faster launches and more creative products in the cosmetics industry. via AI News.

AI costs are plummeting, with capabilities like GPT-4 now under $1 per million tokens, opening doors to near-free intelligence for everyday tasks. This shift will transform data systems as they adapt to manage and interact with swarms of agents. via BAIR Berkeley.

AI chip maker SambaNova has secured $1B in funding, valuing the company at $11B just five months after a previous major round. This highlights the growing demand for AI technology and the competitive landscape among chip manufacturers. via TechCrunch AI

Meta launched Muse Image, a new AI generator for creating images, but users are unhappy about how their photos are being used. This raises concerns about consent and ownership in the age of AI. via TechCrunch AI
Open source AI is thriving, but it's not negatively impacting companies like Anthropic for now. Both open source and frontier labs are serving different stages of AI development. via TechCrunch AI

Microsoft is scaling back on AI spending by focusing more on its own models. This move reflects a growing trend among tech giants to reduce costs while still advancing AI development. via TechCrunch AI

Discord acknowledged a bug in its AI moderation that wrongly banned users for harmless images, affecting accounts since May. This matters because it highlights the risks of relying on AI for content moderation. via TechCrunch AI

Claude Cowork now lets users manage tasks across mobile and web, allowing them to start on their desk and finish on their phone. This update enhances flexibility and productivity for users on the go. via TechCrunch AI

Savi just raised $7 million to launch its app that protects users from realistic AI scams, like fake kidnappers demanding ransom. This could be a game changer in helping consumers stay safe from advanced AI threats. via TechCrunch AI
